segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There’s no time to explain. The beam of a Nutcracker's brass lantern is already sweeping across the brick wall fifty feet away.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You sprint forward, grab the trailing tail of the fox's long red scarf, and give it a firm yank!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You pull the fox sideways behind the wide green dumpster just as the lantern beam cuts through the snow where he was standing!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox lands on your boots, his cap knocked down over his eyes. For a second, he panics in pure, unscripted terror:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: I DON'T TASTE GOOD! I'M MOSTLY FLUFF AND BAD ATTITUDE!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you whisper into his furry ear, pointing toward the mouth of the alley.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peering through the gap between the dumpster and the wall, the fox watches as four stiff-legged Nutcrackers march past, their brass bayonets gleaming in the snow.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The fox pushes his hat out of his eyes. He looks at you, looks at the soldiers, and nods with dignified gravity:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Ahem. An adequate flanking maneuver. I allowed you to execute it to bolster your youthful self-esteem. You may thank me later.
